newsitem.title: USA: Dombeck named U.S. Forest Service chief.
newsitem.headline: Dombeck named U.S. Forest Service chief.

text.p: Michael Dombeck, a high-ranking Interior Department official, was named Friday to be the head of the U.S. Forest Service, overseeing 191 million acres of national forest.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, announcing the appointment at a news conference, called Dombeck a "unifying figure".

For the past two years, Dombeck, 48, was acting director of the Bureau of Land Management in the Interior Department. He worked for the Forest Service for 11 years, eventually becoming its national fisheries program manager before shifting to the BLM in 1989.
As Forest Service chief, Dombeck will face the challenge of balancing logging with recreation and natural resource preservation.
Dombeck, who is from Wisconsin, succeeds Jack Ward Thomas who resigned in October to take a university teaching position.
